_note: Two layers. (1) Index: each stage lists the broad syllabus area(s) it sits in (covers_syllabus_refs / syllabus_topic, as the source spec names them). (2) Coverage: _syllabus_items is the specification broken into its own atomic items, and each stage lists the item ids it teaches in covers_items, so coverage_check.py can say whether the WHOLE specification is taught. Top-level keys starting with _ are metadata, never stages.

_meta.semantics: covers_syllabus_refs is an index of the areas a stage is principally associated with; it does not claim exhaustive coverage of those areas, exam weighting, or official stage boundaries. Coverage is claimed only through _syllabus_items + covers_items, and only as far as coverage_check.py confirms (declared coverage, not verified teaching).

_items_source.document: AQA GCSE English Literature 8702 specification: sections 3.1 (Shakespeare and the 19th-century novel: 3.1.1 Shakespeare, 3.1.2 the 19th-century novel), 3.2 (Modern texts and poetry: 3.2.1 Modern texts, 3.2.2 Poetry, 3.2.3 Unseen poetry), 3.3 (Skills), 4.1-4.3 (Aims, Assessment objectives, Assessment weightings); plus the Paper 1/Paper 2 question format and mark splits from AQA's published mark schemes
_items_source.version: Version 1.3, 28 September 2022 (numbering follows the spec's own section numbers 3.1-3.3 and 4.1-4.3; within each set text the act/stave-by-act/stave, theme, character, language, structure and exam-question items are course-defined ids, e.g. MAC.1 for Macbeth Act 1, ACC.1 for A Christmas Carol Stave 1, IC.1 for An Inspector Calls Act 1, POE.1-POE.15 for the Power and Conflict poems in the anthology's own running order, and UNS.1-3 for unseen poetry; unselected set-text and cluster options are given ids prefixed with the studied text's id plus .X, e.g. MAC.X.RJ for Romeo and Juliet)
